title: The North Face Spectrum 23 review: light and wind-strong, with a condensation problem
dek: A 3 lb 12 oz two-person tent with mixed 10.5 mm and 9 mm poles. Owners like the weight and wind stability, and many fought condensation.
subject: The North Face Spectrum 23
verdict: The Spectrum 23 is light, compact and quick to pitch, and owners say it handles strong wind well. Its big weakness is condensation: many owners woke to water running down the walls or pooling on the floor. It's a better solo tent than a two-person one.
bestFor: Solo backpackers in dry or breezy climates who want a light, fast tent.
notFor: Humid or calm conditions, two tall people, or anyone sensitive to a damp morning.

body:
## The short version

The Spectrum 23 is a light two-person tent with three poles in two sizes, 10.5 mm and 9 mm. Owners on Trailspace like the light weight, small pack size and fast setup, and say it handles strong wind well. It averages middling ratings because of one problem: condensation.

## Condensation

Several owners woke up to water pooling on the floor and running down the walls, especially when camping solo, in humid conditions or on calm nights. Some found that adjusting the front flaps and vents helped; others found it hard to fix. Owners also report the floor soaking up moisture, so a footprint is a must.

## Space

Two people fit, but owners call it cramped for two or for taller users. As a solo tent with room for gear, it makes more sense.

## Weather

Wind is its strength. Owners report it holding well in strong wind, which fits its light, tensioned design.

## Poles and parts

The Spectrum 23 uses **3 poles**, **10.5 mm and 9 mm** tubing (thicker and thinner poles in the same set).

The Spectrum's poles come in two diameters, 10.5 mm and 9 mm, so match both the diameter and the length when replacing one.

The North Face doesn't publish pole lengths. To match a replacement, lay your pole out straight, measure tip to tip, count the sections, and read the diameter printed near a joint (or use calipers). Then search the Spectrum 23 in our [pole and parts finder](/poles?model=Spectrum%2023), compare against measured stock in the [pole size chart](/poles/sizes), or search by measurement in [find a pole by size](/poles/size).

## Bottom line

If you camp solo in dry or breezy places, a used Spectrum 23 is a light, capable tent. In humid or still conditions, ventilate aggressively or choose something else.
